applies_why: The judge text addresses whether Jeremiah 22:30/C4 counts against a link, which is the unanswered-witness counting that K-G4 governs.
quote: D6 vs C4 (Jeremiah 22:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- C4 pressed against the curse limb the defender dropped in [CR3] LINK 5, so no live link remains to contradict; the dropping is recorded there.
rule_words: A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it. Not counting it obeys this rule.
room: counts as an unanswered witness only when: reading one, the judge counts C4 toward a broken link and must quote the earlier pressing sentence; reading two, the judge does not count it because the pressed limb was dropped, which the rule allows.
why: The judge does not count Jeremiah 22:30 as an unanswered witness toward a broken link; it says no live link remains because the limb was dropped, and not counting it obeys K-G4.
